prompt:
Analyze the following external review that has been addressed.
Identify what our INTERNAL code review should have caught
BEFORE the external reviewer found it.

## External Review Feedback


## Code Comments (with Resolutions)
- [operators/keystone/internal/controller/keystone_controller.go:577] Do not reference prior implementation details in code comments. Nobody evaluating the new code will know or care about how it was once implemented. Only document current behavior and behavior that could look odd for someone looking at the code for the first time.
- [operators/keystone/internal/controller/keystone_controller_test.go:2793] Do not test for constant value literals

## Resolution Summary
Both review comments were addressed directly at the cited locations. The doc comment on `secretToKeystoneMapper` was rewritten to document only current behavior — the paragraph describing how the new path 'replaces the prior unfiltered namespace-scoped List' and the 'review #1' parenthetical references were removed, while the still-relevant rationale (owner-ref scoping, cached Get for stale refs) was retained with REQ tags. In the owner-ref group-match test, the assertion against the `ks.Name` constant literal was dropped, leaving only the `HaveLen(1)` behavioral check. No changes were made outside the two locations called out in the review.

Extract 0-3 review improvement patterns. For each:
- name: Short, action-oriented name IN ENGLISH
- review_area: error-handling | security | testing | performance | type-safety | validation | architecture | naming | documentation
- detection_hint: How should the reviewer detect this?
- severity: BLOCKING | WARNING
- what_to_check: What exactly to check
- why_it_matters: Why it matters
- example_feedback: Original quote from the reviewer
- example_fix: What was changed

QUALITY: Only real review blindspots. No subjective style opinions.
Nothing that only a domain expert could know.
If nothing extractable: empty array.

LANGUAGE: ALL fields MUST be in English.

Response: ONLY JSON array.
